title: Dyskeratosis congenita (telomerase defect): hematopoietic stem cell failure
vignette: An 18-year-old man is evaluated for fatigue and easy bruising. On examination he has premature graying of the hair, white plaques on the oral mucosa (oral leukoplakia), lacy reticulated hyperpigmentation of the skin, and dystrophic, abnormally formed fingernails. His mother has idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Complete blood count shows pancytopenia. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the gene encoding telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT). Failure of which of the following cell populations best explains this patient's cytopenias?

clues.note: Oral leukoplakia is one of the classic diagnostic triad of dyskeratosis congenita (with nail dystrophy and reticulated hyperpigmentation).

clues.text: lacy reticulated hyperpigmentation of the skin
clues.note: Reticulated skin hyperpigmentation is the second element of the dyskeratosis congenita triad.
Nail dystrophy completes the classic dyskeratosis congenita triad (nails, oral leukoplakia, reticulated pigmentation).
Pancytopenia (low counts in all three lineages) reflects failure of the multipotent hematopoietic stem cells that supply the marrow.

clues.text: mutation in the gene encoding telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT)
clues.note: A TERT (telomerase) mutation impairs telomere maintenance; rapidly dividing tissues (bone marrow) exhaust their proliferative capacity first, causing marrow failure.

whatMatters: Nail dystrophy + oral leukoplakia + reticulated skin hyperpigmentation + a telomerase (TERT) mutation = dyskeratosis congenita, a telomere-maintenance disorder. Because telomerase is essential for highly proliferative tissues, the rapidly dividing HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS fail first, producing pancytopenia/aplastic anemia. Answer D.
strategy: Recognize dyskeratosis congenita (mucocutaneous triad + telomerase mutation + marrow failure ± family pulmonary fibrosis). Then reason that short-telomere disease hits the MOST proliferative cell population - hematopoietic stem cells - explaining pancytopenia. Reject terminally differentiated, non-dividing cells (cardiac myocytes, neurons, skeletal muscle) and mature lymphocytes (downstream, not the failing stem pool).

eliminations.label: Cardiac myocytes - non-dividing, not the source of cytopenias
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: terminally differentiated heart muscle cells that rarely divide. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: their low turnover makes them relatively spared by telomerase deficiency, and they don't produce blood cells. ✅ Correct if: a cardiomyopathy question, not marrow failure.

eliminations.label: Mature lymphocytes - downstream, not the failing stem pool
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: differentiated circulating lymphocytes. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: pancytopenia (all three lineages) reflects failure UPSTREAM at the multipotent stem cell, not the mature lymphocyte compartment. ✅ Correct if: an isolated lymphocyte problem, not tri-lineage cytopenia.

eliminations.label: Neurons - post-mitotic, not blood-forming
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: largely non-dividing nerve cells. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they have minimal proliferation and don't generate blood cells, so their telomeres are not the cause of pancytopenia. ✅ Correct if: a neurodegenerative process.

eliminations.label: Skeletal muscle cells - low turnover, unrelated to blood counts
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: differentiated skeletal myofibers with low proliferative demand. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they are relatively spared by short telomeres and don't produce blood cells. ✅ Correct if: a myopathy question, not marrow failure.

reasoning: Nail dystrophy + oral leukoplakia + reticulated hyperpigmentation + TERT mutation = dyskeratosis congenita
Telomerase (TERT) maintains telomeres; its deficiency limits how many times a cell can divide
The most proliferative tissue - bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells - exhausts first
-> hematopoietic stem cell failure -> pancytopenia; answer D
mechanism: Telomeres are repetitive TTAGGG caps that shorten with each cell division; telomerase (a reverse transcriptase whose catalytic subunit is TERT, with the RNA template TERC) re-extends them, preserving replicative capacity in stem and germ cells. Dyskeratosis congenita is caused by mutations in telomere-maintenance genes (e.g., TERT, TERC, DKC1), producing abnormally short telomeres. Tissues with the highest proliferative demand fail first: the bone marrow's hematopoietic stem cells exhaust their replicative potential, causing progressive marrow failure (pancytopenia/aplastic anemia) - the leading cause of death. The classic mucocutaneous triad is nail dystrophy, oral leukoplakia, and reticulated skin hyperpigmentation; patients also have increased risk of pulmonary fibrosis and malignancy, and short-telomere syndromes can present in relatives as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (as in this patient's mother). Terminally differentiated, low-turnover cells (cardiac myocytes, neurons, skeletal muscle) are relatively spared, and mature lymphocytes are downstream of the failing stem-cell pool.

difficulty.message: First Aid Biochem/Heme > telomerase (TERT/TERC), telomeres; dyskeratosis congenita (nail dystrophy, oral leukoplakia, reticulated hyperpigmentation) -> bone marrow (hematopoietic stem cell) failure, pulmonary fibrosis, cancer risk.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: Short-telomere disease strikes the most proliferative pool first - hematopoietic stem cells - explaining pancytopenia.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on telomere/telomerase, TERT vs TERC, dyskeratosis congenita triad, or hematopoietic stem cell? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Cardiac myocytes, neurons, and skeletal muscle are low-turnover/post-mitotic; mature lymphocytes are downstream - none accounts for tri-lineage cytopenia.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: dyskeratosis congenita = telomerase defect -> hematopoietic stem cell failure (pancytopenia); triad = nails, oral leukoplakia, reticulated pigment; + pulmonary fibrosis.
